solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fruit on bus heading west very nice indeed

indicators.note: in an across answer, heading west means travelling right to left, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written, before it turns round
a lime is a green citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a piece of fruit on a westbound bus and finds it delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in an across clue puts the fruit after the reversed bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime describes something of supreme excellence or beauty, a strong way of praising it.

clue.text: Woman regularly soused

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every other one starting with the first

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of soused

explanation.surface: A woman who is often drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a female first name, and crosswords often clue any given name as woman or man.

clue.text: Governing body and editor got on

blocks.note: a board of directors or governors runs an organisation
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper's directors and its editor got along well together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got on' suggests getting along with people; here it means climbing onto a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a ship, train or bus is to climb onto it, so having boarded is having got on.

clue.text: Increasingly sick murderer losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: a killer is a murderer

explanation.surface: A murderer grows sicker and then is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Iller is the comparative form of ill, meaning more unwell, so it matches a phrase describing worsening health.

clue.text: Very quick to communicate

blocks.note: first meaning: fast, as an ... train or delivery
second meaning: to put thoughts or feelings into words

explanation.surface: Someone is very fast at getting a message across.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for a fast service and a verb for conveying a thought or feeling.

clue.text: Restrain two females going after copper

indicators.note: going after means following behind, so the females are placed second in the line

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
F is the abbreviation for female, taken twice

explanation.surface: Two women chase a policeman and try to hold him back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal; 'going after' puts the females second.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuff someone is to put handcuffs on them, which holds them back physically.

clue.text: Actors initially enjoy class

indicators.note: initially points at the very start of the word it follows, keeping only its opening letter

blocks.note: the cast is the set of actors in a show
the opening letter of enjoy

explanation.surface: Actors at first enjoy their drama lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social rank, especially in the Hindu system, so it is a social group or stratum.

clue.text: Drunken street oaf getting warning

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk lout in the street gets told off.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample of something to come, so it serves as an advance hint or signal.

clue.text: Alien found in Irish parliament? It’s a fact!

indicators.note: found in says one thing sits inside another, so one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament
ET is the film alien, standard crossword shorthand for an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone claims, as a matter of fact, that an extraterrestrial has turned up in the Irish parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil Éireann is the main chamber of Ireland's parliament; the question mark flags the fanciful scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a single item of information or particular point, which is what an individual fact is.

clue.text: Old man’s attempt to make a cake?

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father, with the possessive s
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Dad has a go at baking a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a cake is only loosely a pastry; the answer is a dough used for pies and tarts, or an individual sweet bake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry is also a single sweet baked item such as a Danish or eclair, so it overlaps with small cakes.

clue.text: Desperate Merton needs support

indicators.note: something desperate is in a frantic state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Merton, in a desperate state, needs backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs' is part of the letter mix as well as reading like a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An endorsement is public approval or backing given to a person, product or cause.

clue.text: Scientist terribly close to GI

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters come out in a muddled order

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A researcher stands very near an American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A GI is an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecologist studies how living things relate to their environment, which is a branch of biological research.

clue.text: Gangster loves to be a bringer of misfortune

blocks.note: hood is slang for a hoodlum or gangster
love is zero in tennis, written as O; two of them here

explanation.surface: A mobster's affections turn out to be unlucky.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a jinx: a person or thing thought to cause bad luck.

clue.text: By whom an autobiography is written?

definitions.text: By whom an autobiography is written?

blocks.clueFragment: By whom an autobiography is written?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question asking which author wrote some life story

blocks.clueFragment: By whom an autobiography is written?
blocks.note: setter's reading: an autobiography is by definition written by its own subject, so the reply is a reflexive pronoun

explanation.walkthrough: The question looks like it wants a writer's name, but every autobiography has the same author: the person it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun names the subject acting on themselves, which is exactly who writes their own life story.

clue.text: Son visiting island state for a bite to eat

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so one word ends up within another

blocks.note: Samoa is an island nation in the South Pacific
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son travels to a Pacific island nation to grab something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried pastry snack with a spiced filling, a typical quick snack.

clue.text: LA detectives turning up to support me in examination

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Los Angeles police officers arrive to back me up during a test.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'to support' puts the reversed piece underneath ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical check-up by a doctor, a health examination.

clue.text: Cheating, as bluegrass musician might be?

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for being dishonest, especially fiddling money
second meaning, read literally: a bluegrass player is often busy playing a violin

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a fiddle is a swindle, so being on it means engaged in fraud; the fiddle is also the violin central to bluegrass music.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means involved in petty fraud, while literally describing someone occupied with playing a violin.

clue.text: Spitting Image entertaining a US novelist

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside your house, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: the spitting image of someone looks exactly like them, as a twin does
taken as written

explanation.surface: The satirical puppet show Spitting Image amuses an American writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Spitting Image was a British TV satire using puppets, but here it is just an exact lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Clemens, the American author of Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Opening succession of Latin letters

indicators.note: a succession of letters is an unbroken run, so the answer is a consecutive string inside the following words

blocks.note: runs across the end of Latin and the start of letters

explanation.surface: The opening sequence of an inscription in Roman characters.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow gap where water enters the coast, or more generally any way in.

clue.text: Nick quietly angry

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical marking for quietly
irate means angry

explanation.surface: Someone named Nick is calmly furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name; it is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pirate is to copy or take something without permission, which is what stealing it means in slang.

clue.text: So cult indecently produces stripper?

indicators.note: indecently suggests improper behaviour, so the letters are disarranged

blocks.note: the six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A sect behaving improperly ends up with an exotic dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripper is not a dancer but an insect that strips fields bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarms of locusts devour every plant in their path, leaving crops and trees bare.

clue.text: Sneaky agent having change of heart

indicators.note: the heart is the middle letter, and changing it means swapping in a different one

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A secret agent changes sides on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: The new middle letter is not clued, so the definition and crossers fix it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly means cunning and secretive, acting in an underhand way.

clue.text: School taken in, by the sound of it

indicators.note: these words say the answer is something that sounds right when spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: food taken in has been eaten

explanation.surface: A school seems to have been fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests being deceived; it means swallowed. Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a well-known English boarding school near Windsor.

clue.text: Disastrously obese friend

blocks.note: obese means very fat
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A very overweight friend causes calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatally means in a way that causes ruin or death, so it describes a catastrophic outcome.
